tagline: A fur-trade town, and a gorge cut into the prairie.
intro: West of Walhalla the backway drops in with the Pembina River and follows its bends through the Pembina Gorge. The valley goes deep here. Water carved it out of soft marine shale, and it is one of the deepest and steepest river valleys in North Dakota, holding about 12,500 acres of oak, birch and thicket.
Walhalla, the second oldest town in the state, began in 1845 as St. Joseph, named for the local Catholic mission, and grew up in the fur trade. From there the road runs south and east to Cavalier.

moments.title: Pembina Gorge State Park
moments.text: Six miles west of Walhalla, North Dakota's 14th state park opened in June 2026 to kayakers and trail riders, in a gorge holding the most rare species known in the state.

moments.title: Frost Fire Park
moments.text: A small ski hill built upside down, with the parking lot and lodge at the top of the runs, where in summer the chairlift carries mountain bikes back up.

moments.title: Walhalla
moments.text: On the Pembina five miles below the Manitoba line, the Kittson Trading Post of 1843 still stands in the state historical park, the oldest building in North Dakota.
